units.text: INT. BARBARA - CONTINUOUS
For instance, what's the matter with that out-patient over there?
units.name: UNDERSHAFT

units.text: BARBARA [looking at Bill, whose attitude has never changed, and whose expression of brooding wrath has deepened] Oh, we shall cure him in no time.
Just watch. [She goes over to Bill and waits.
He glances up at her and casts his eyes down again, uneasy, but grimmer than ever].
It would be nice to just stamp on Mog Habbijam's face, wouldn't it, Bill?
BILL [starting up from the trough in consternation] It's a lie: I never said so. [She shakes her head].
Who told you wot was in my mind?
Only your new friend.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Wot new friend?
units.name: BILL

units.text: The devil, Bill. When he gets round people they get miserable, just like you.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: HILL [with a heartbreaking attempt at devil-may-care cheerfulness] I ain't miserable. [He sits down again, and stretches his legs in an attempt to seem indifferent].
Well, if you're happy, why don't you look happy, as we do?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [his legs curling back in spite of him] I'm appy enough, I tell you.
Why don't you lea me alown?
Wot av I done to you?
I ain't smashed your face, av I?
BARBARA [softly: wooing his soul] It's not me that's getting at you, Bill.
Who else is it?
units.name: BILL

units.text: Somebody that doesn't intend you to smash women's faces, I suppose. Somebody or something that wants to make a man of you.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [blustering] Make a man o ME!
Ain't I a man? eh? ain't I a man?
Who sez I'm not a man?
There's a man in you somewhere, I suppose. But why did he let you hit poor little Jenny Hill? That wasn't very manly of him, was it?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [tormented] Av done with it, I tell you.
Chock it.
I'm sick of your Jenny Ill and er silly little face.
Then why do you keep thinking about it? Why does it keep coming up against you in your mind? You're not getting converted, are you?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [with conviction] Not ME.
Not likely.
Not arf.

That's right, Bill. Hold out against it. Put out your strength. Don't let's get you cheap. Todger Fairmile said he wrestled for three nights against his Salvation harder than he ever wrestled with the Jap at the music hall. He gave in to the Jap when his arm was going to break. But he didn't give in to his salvation until his heart was going to break. Perhaps you'll escape that. You haven't any heart, have you?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Wot dye mean? Wy ain't I got a art the same as ennybody else?
units.name: BILL

units.text: A man with a heart wouldn't have bashed poor little Jenny's face, would he?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [almost crying] Ow, will you lea me alown?
Av I ever offered to meddle with you, that you come noggin and provowkin me lawk this? [He writhes convulsively from his eyes to his toes].
BARBARA [with a steady soothing hand on his arm and a gentle voice that never lets him go] It's your soul that's hurting you, Bill, and not me.
We've been through it all ourselves.
Come with us, Bill. [He looks wildly round].
To brave manhood on earth and eternal glory in heaven. [He is on the point of breaking down].
Come. [A drum is heard in the shelter; and Bill, with a gasp, escapes from the spell as Barbara turns quickly.
Adolphus enters from the shelter with a big drum].
Oh! there you are, Dolly.
Let me introduce a new friend of mine, Mr Bill Walker.
This is my bloke, Bill: Mr Cusins. [Cusins salutes with his drumstick].
Goin to marry im?
units.name: BILL

units.text: Yes.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [fervently] Gawd elp im!
Gawd elp im!
Why? Do you think he won't be happy with me?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: I've only ad to stand it for a mornin: e'll av to stand it for a lifetime.
units.name: BILL

units.text: That is a frightful reflection, Mr Walker. But I can't tear myself away from her.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Well, I can.
units.name: BILL

units.text: To Barbara.
Eah! do you know where I'm goin to, and wot I'm goin to do?
units.name: BILL

units.text: Yes: you're going to heaven; and you're coming back here before the week's out to tell me so.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: You lie. I'm goin to Kennintahn, to spit in Todger Fairmile's eye. I bashed Jenny Ill's face; and now I'll get me own face bashed and come back and show it to er. E'll it me ardern I it er. That'll make us square.
units.name: BILL

units.text: To Adolphus.
Is that fair or is it not? You're a genlmn: you oughter know.
units.name: BILL

units.text: Two black eyes wont make one white one, Bill.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: I didn't ast you. Cawn't you never keep your mahth shut? I ast the genlmn.
units.name: BILL

units.text: CUSINS [reflectively] Yes: I think you're right, Mr Walker.
Yes: I should do it.
It's curious: it's exactly what an ancient Greek would have done.
But what good will it do?
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: Well, it will give Mr Fairmile some exercise; and it will satisfy Mr Walker's soul.
units.name: CUSINS

units.text: Rot! there ain't no sach a thing as a soul. Ah kin you tell wether I've a soul or not? You never seen it.
units.name: BILL

units.text: I've seen it hurting you when you went against it.
units.name: BARBARA

units.text: BILL [with compressed aggravation] If you was my girl and took the word out o me mahth lawk thet, I'd give you suthink you'd feel urtin, so I would. [To Adolphus] You take my tip, mate.
Stop er jawr; or you'll die afore your time. [With intense expression] Wore aht: thets wot you'll be: wore aht. [He goes away through the gate].
CUSINS [looking after him] I wonder!
Dolly!
units.name: BARBARA
